page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.14xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on KVM virtualization and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance allocates 56 dedicated virtual CPUs across 28 physical cores, maintaining a 2:1 thread-to-core ratio. The memory architecture supplies 224.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU configuration provides a 35 MB L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2. This server includes 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates with no local bundled storage, and does not provide GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests register in the lower tiers, including a Geekbench single-core score of 948.0, a stress-ng single-core rating of 1107.38, and a poor single-threaded gzip compression speed of 19.05 GB/sec. Conversely, parallel execution benefits from the 56 dedicated vCPUs, yielding average-tier metrics such as 40954.08 in stress-ng multi-core, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9467.0, and 172.5 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. PassMark CPU testing logged 35028.65, while memory subsystem evaluation demonstrated 104.82 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 50.54 GB/sec in uncached writes.

In operational benchmarks, the server handles shared memory and throughput tasks reliably, delivering 38.16 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 21.94 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. PassMark database operations scored 14811.15. For language model execution without hardware accelerators, small model prompt processing reached 1908.49 tokens per second, though text generation was limited to 46.57 tokens per second. Because there is no bundled local storage, persistent and scratch volumes require attached remote storage.

The ecs.sn2ne.14xlarge provides solid density for highly threaded enterprise workloads requiring standard memory allocations, such as multi-threaded backend services, enterprise application tiers, distributed caching, and static web delivery. It represents a less cost-effective fit for single-thread bound routines, I/O workloads demanding low-latency local disks, or intensive neural network text generation.
